name: skipfish
summary: A fully automated, active web application security reconnaissance tool.
highlights: -N — - do not accept any new cookies
-P — - do not parse HTML, etc, to find new links
usage: skipfish [ options ... ] -W wordlist -o output_dir start_url [ start_url2 ... ]

flags.name: -N
flags.description: - do not accept any new cookies

flags.name: --auth-form
flags.description: - form authentication URL

flags.name: -I
flags.description: - only follow URLs matching 'string'

flags.name: -X
flags.description: - exclude URLs matching 'string'

flags.name: -K
flags.description: - do not fuzz parameters named 'string'

flags.name: -Z
flags.description: - do not descend into 5xx locations

flags.name: -O
flags.description: - do not submit any forms

flags.name: -P
flags.description: - do not parse HTML, etc, to find new links

flags.name: -o
flags.description: - write output to specified directory (required)

flags.name: -M
flags.description: - log warnings about mixed content / non-SSL passwords

flags.name: -E
flags.description: - log all HTTP/1.0 / HTTP/1.1 caching intent mismatches

flags.name: -U
flags.description: - log all external URLs and e-mails seen

flags.name: -Q
flags.description: - completely suppress duplicate nodes in reports

flags.name: -u
flags.description: - be quiet, disable realtime progress stats

flags.name: -v
flags.description: - enable runtime logging (to stderr)

flags.name: -L
flags.description: - do not auto-learn new keywords for the site

flags.name: -Y
flags.description: - do not fuzz extensions in directory brute-force

flags.name: -e
flags.description: - do not keep binary responses for reporting

flags.name: -k
flags.description: - stop scanning after the given duration h:m:s

flags.name: --config
flags.description: - load the specified configuration file
